nodes.name: Giveaway and Entry-Point Backlog

nodes.languageNotes: Markdown table format with hyperlinks to related documentation and live URLs

nodes.name: Giveaway Launch Workflow
nodes.summary: Complete end-to-end process for delivering free lead magnets, skills, and resources to attract and qualify leads. Three phases: Technical Setup, Content Creation, and Publishing.

nodes.name: Phase 1: Technical Setup
nodes.summary: Technical foundation for launching a giveaway including page creation, registry registration, deployment to production, and verification.

nodes.name: Phase 2: Content Creation
nodes.summary: Content and hook generation using HookLab for creating engaging Instagram reels. Includes hook writing (Pass 1: CTA First) and full script generation (Pass 2).

nodes.name: Phase 3: Publishing
nodes.summary: Publishing and activation of giveaway content on Instagram and ManyChat automation verification.

nodes.name: Giveaway Template Structure
nodes.summary: Hardened template requirements for giveaway pages including 14 required elements: client directive, animations, particles, gradients, fonts, badges, buttons, testimonials, CTA blocks, reactions, attribution, theme, and scroll effects.

nodes.name: Giveaway Email Collection Pattern
nodes.summary: Email capture mechanism for converting giveaway visitors into leads. Includes modal component (GiveawayEmailModal / GiveawayAutoModal), submission contract to /api/lead-magnet, regex validation, and rate limiting.

nodes.name: ManyChat Automation Setup
nodes.summary: Instagram comment automation for giveaway delivery. Comment trigger on keyword, DM ask for email, email capture, and delivery message with link. Manual flow creation via ManyChat UI using MASTER template clone.

nodes.name: The Cost Stack Audit Giveaway
nodes.summary: Live giveaway (LIVE since 2026-08-03, slug: cost-stack). A calculator-type entry point that helps identify cost leakage. Keyword: STACK. Automatable: 5/5. Effort: 1 review pass. Discovered email delivery production bug during launch.

nodes.name: Bring the Task You Hate Giveaway
nodes.summary: Free live workshop/hot-seat (LIVE Sept 29 2026, slug: bring-the-task-you-hate). Originally proposed 2026-09-16, runs as 'Free AI Class: Bring the Task You Hate the Most. Leave Without It.' 56 signups on July 29 run, 7 net-new C4 qualified. Zero prep required—intake answers serve as run sheet.

nodes.name: Make AI Sound Like You Giveaway
nodes.summary: Free live workshop/build-along (NEXT status, slug: stop-sounding-like-everyone-else). Focuses on voice profile + Speak Human. 90 min live delivery. Aug 4 run got 10 signups on two days promo. Needs 10-14 days runway plus Marina ref link.

nodes.name: Clone guardog Rule
nodes.summary: Template selection rule: clone guardog (not benchmark, not compare) regardless of content type. Structure determines template, not content. Benchmark and compare pre-date hardened template and are non-conforming.

nodes.name: Email Modal Trigger Pattern
nodes.summary: Universal requirement for giveaway pages. Copy-prompt pages open modal on Copy button. Non-copy-prompt pages auto-open after 20-second delay, suppressed by sessionStorage for once-per-session delivery.

nodes.name: GiveawayAutoModal Component
nodes.summary: Reusable component (src/components/giveaways/GiveawayAutoModal.tsx) that encapsulates auto-popup state, timer, sessionStorage, and email collection for non-copy-prompt giveaway pages. Replaces verbose inline pattern.

nodes.name: Three Delivery Edits Rule
nodes.summary: Creating a giveaway requires three file edits: page file, registry entry (giveaways.ts), and delivery template entry plus slug in lead-magnets.ts. Missing any one silently breaks the email delivery path.

nodes.name: Resend Email Delivery Bug (2026-08-03)
nodes.summary: Production incident: all giveaway delivery emails failed with Resend 422 error. Root cause: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL had trailing newline, which broke the List-Unsubscribe header. Fixed by trimming/stripping CR/LF in getSiteUrl(). Guard tests added to prevent recurrence.

nodes.name: Giveaway Mobile Design Rules
nodes.summary: Mobile-specific requirements for giveaway pages including badge positioning (relative z-10 on mobile, absolute sm:top-10), aurora blob sizes (320px mobile, 500px sm, 600px md), code block text wrapping, and section padding (px-5 py-8 sm:px-8 sm:py-10).

nodes.name: HookLab Integration
nodes.summary: Two-pass hook and reel script generation. Pass 1 (CTA First mode) generates 15 hook candidates scored on 5 axes (Concreteness, Mechanism, Voice, Self-recognition, Thumb stop). Pass 2 generates full 45s reel script with on-screen callouts, delivery notes, and Instagram caption.

nodes.name: Giveaway Pre-flight Checklist
nodes.summary: Four uniqueness checks before launching: slug directory, registry entry, ManyChat keyword, and git repo cleanliness. All must pass before touching any files.

nodes.summary: Canonical delivery domain is https://workshop.mastermindshq.business/giveaways/<slug>. Legacy domain https://workshop-site-sigma.vercel.app/ still works but should be phased out. Domain consistency is outstanding across all giveaway rows.

tour.title: Application Overview
tour.description: Start with the root App Router layout to see how Masterminds workshop content receives shared metadata, typography and site chrome. The package manifest establishes the Next.js and React application and its Stripe, Supabase, Resend and Google API integrations, which support registration, payments and resource delivery throughout this tour.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js App Router layouts wrap routed pages, allowing shared document and interface behavior to remain separate from individual feature pages.

tour.title: Routing and Packaging
tour.description: With the application shell in view, inspect the Next.js configuration to understand how visitors reach dedicated landing pages and how legacy session and resource links move to the portal. Output tracing also includes private prompt-pack assets, connecting deployment packaging to the authenticated downloads introduced later.

tour.title: Consent Across Experiences
tour.description: The layout directly imports the React consent manager, which uses shared region, host and cookie rules before initializing browser tracking. The regional API and standalone HTML consent bootstrap extend those rules across routed pages and static resources, so checkout attribution and verified purchases depend on the same consent decisions.

tour.title: Event Catalog and Intake
tour.description: Move from the shared shell to an event page, where the event catalog supplies event details, prices and upcoming live sessions. Intake validation and checkout-payload helpers turn visitor information into the structured registration request consumed by the server in the next step.

tour.title: Registration and Checkout
tour.description: The checkout route coordinates request validation, seat reservations and payment creation instead of treating payment as an isolated action. Capacity helpers track reservation transitions, while the checkout builder creates branded Stripe sessions with attendee and attribution metadata; the same route can finalize a free registration and coordinate confirmation and calendar delivery.

tour.title: Persistence and Access Controls
tour.description: The registration database layer connects the enrollment flow to durable registrations, cancellations, intake and waitlists through Supabase. Read the migrations alongside it to distinguish self-reported AI grades from assessed grades and attendance, and to see how intake access is restricted through row-level security while server service access is retained.
tour.languageLesson: SQL migrations describe changes to persisted data and privileges. Row-level security and role grants must be understood together when tracing which application credentials may access a table.

tour.title: Subscription Product Flow
tour.description: The AI Agent Income sales page is a second commercial journey built alongside event checkout. Its email form starts a rate-limited Stripe subscription checkout with a seven-day trial, while the webhook verifies and deduplicates incoming events before reconciling subscriptions and delivering subscriber resources.

tour.title: Protected Resource Delivery
tour.description: Follow the subscription journey into prompt-pack access to see why private assets were included in output tracing earlier. A request must match an active subscription, signed expiring links carry the download authorization, and the download route validates the token and subscription email before streaming the ZIP.

tour.title: Giveaways and Lead Capture
tour.description: Giveaway routes now supply typed pack content to a shared rendering component. Trace copying and downloads through the post-action email request, including direct-message visitor exemptions and the once-per-tab rule.

tour.title: Pack Content and Offers
tour.description: The Lead Machine pack shows how resource copy, prompts, downloads, and navigation are defined separately from the template. Free AI tools adapt their shared catalog into the same shape, while offer selection follows the declared AI level.

tour.title: Giveaway Email Delivery
tour.description: Follow a resource request into the lead magnet API and the generic giveaway email builder. Source validation, safe destination handling, rate limits, suppression checks, and idempotency control delivery without exposing free resources behind an email form.

tour.title: Content Launch Standards
tour.description: The giveaway launch protocol explains how the preceding components become a released resource, from canonical templates and email collection through deployment, grading and publishing. The usefulness rubric supplies the release criteria, while the standalone playbook deck and interactive coaching matrix illustrate the static educational experiences that share consent handling.

tour.title: Behavioral Verification
tour.description: Now inspect tests that exercise the boundaries established by the previous steps: event pricing and checkout modes, consent metadata, resource delivery, signed prompt-pack access and database intake security. These suites provide examples of observable contracts and mocked integration behavior; the package test commands determine how the available checks are invoked.

tour.title: Deployment and Scheduled Operations
tour.description: Finish with Vercel configuration to connect the application journeys to production routing and scheduled operations. Host rewrites select product landing pages, while cron schedules invoke event follow-up, reminder and reconciliation routes; the package manifest supplies the runtime requirement and development, build and test commands used around that deployment.
